answer:
Here is what I would raise, most important first.

1. Your stool blood test (FIT) on 2025-11-04 was POSITIVE, and I can find nothing after it: no colonoscopy, no referral, no repeat test. A positive FIT should be followed by a colonoscopy, and it is now about a year later. This is the one item I would not let wait. Ask your doctor whether a colonoscopy was ordered or done somewhere else, and get it scheduled if not.

2. Diabetes follow-up. Your last A1c was 6.9% on 2026-02-16, which is good compared with the 8.3% in January 2025. But it is more than 8 months old, and A1c is usually checked every 3 to 6 months, so one is due. Your records also show no urine albumin (kidney) test, eye exam or foot exam, which are normally done yearly with diabetes. They may have been done elsewhere, so ask.

3. Cholesterol. Your only cholesterol panel is from 2025-02-18: LDL 131 (above the 99 listed limit) and total 212. Atorvastatin 20 mg was prescribed two days later. There is no repeat panel to show whether it worked, so ask for one.

4. Things that may look odd. Metformin was ended on 2024-04-15 with no reason recorded; your A1c then climbed from 6.7% to 8.3% by January 2025, and Jardiance (empagliflozin) was started 2025-02-20 and is still listed as active. Your chart also contains a 'pulmonary embolism' entry from 2025-07-08, but it is marked refuted: the CT scan that day showed no clot, and the D-dimer was raised (0.92) but that alone is not diagnostic. The visit ended as chest wall pain, which resolved. Make sure the pulmonary embolism entry is not being read as a real diagnosis.

5. Kidney function (eGFR 73 in 2025, 69 in Feb 2026) is normal but has drifted slightly down; it is worth rechecking since you take Jardiance.

I can only see the records provided; anything done elsewhere would not show up.
short: Positive FIT on 2025-11-04 with no recorded colonoscopy or follow-up; A1c (last 6.9% in Feb 2026) and lipids (LDL 131 in Feb 2025, no recheck on atorvastatin) are due; the refuted pulmonary embolism entry should not be read as a diagnosis.
